passages.text: In the published credits for *ଛ’ ମାଣ ଆଠ ଗୁଣ୍ଠ (Chha Mana Atha Guntha)*, Parbati Ghose appears as producer, director and performer. The screenplay and dialogue are credited to Shrabani, identified there as Parbati Ghose. The archive dates this adaptation of Fakir Mohan Senapati’s novel to 1986.

In the adaptation, Parbati played Saria, Bijay Mohanty played Bhagia and Sarat Pujari played Mangaraj. The archive names Ashok Swain for camera, Tapas Mukherjee for editing and Prafulla Kar for music.
Gour–Parbati archive, Chha Mana Atha Guntha (1986), production, screenplay, cast and technical credits.

The archive dates her *ଛ’ ମାଣ ଆଠ ଗୁଣ୍ଠ (Chha Mana Atha Guntha)* adaptation to 1986. Its credits name **Nagen Barik** for sound and **Asim Basu and Sarat Sahoo** for art, and acknowledge Olosingh’s villagers and host **Kalyani Patnaik**. The Parbati Ghose companion follows her producing, writing, directing and acting work.

The *Chha Mana Atha Guntha* archive names **Kalinga Studio** and **Prasad Film Laboratory** among its credits, while stating that the shoot took place entirely in Olosingh. The credits do not specify which services those facilities supplied.
Gour–Parbati archive, *Chha Mana Atha Guntha* (1986), story, direction, screenplay and cast credits.

Mohapatra’s own note, reproduced in the Bologna programme, describes married sons balancing competing responsibilities and daughters-in-law seeking freedom within the household. His interest held affection and frustration together: family could offer warmth while also constraining the people who lived within it.
The negative had been found abandoned in a warehouse in poor condition, according to Film Heritage Foundation’s Shivendra Singh Dungarpur in the Bologna programme.
Bologna’s programme also credits the director’s family, Digital Film Restore for digital restoration, and Prasad Corporation for scanning.
The restoration was screened at Il Cinema Ritrovato in Bologna on 27 June 2024.
Prabha, the eldest son Tuku’s wife, is played by Manaswini Mangaraj.
Il Cinema Ritrovato, Māyā Miriga, 2024 programme, 27 June screening.
On 27 June 2024, *ମାୟା ମିରିଗ (Maya Miriga)* returned to a screen in Bologna, restored after its negative was found badly damaged.
Nirad Mohapatra’s film asks what family gives its members—and what it withholds. His programme note holds warmth alongside daughters-in-law’s desire for freedom.
Il Cinema Ritrovato, Māyā Miriga, 2024 programme, screening date, filmmaker’s note and restoration account.

Uttam Mohanty recalled meeting Meher, who photographed him and cast him in *Abhiman*. In the 2018 interview, Mohanty described obtaining his family’s permission and completing the shoot in 35 days. The recollection supplies an actor’s account of entering a production Meher directed.
Actor, Heartthrob, Superstar. Jyoti Prakash Sahoo, MyCityLinks, 15 July 2018; Uttam Mohanty’s recollection.
Technology also appears in performers’ memories. Uttam Mohanty contrasted reflector-lit shoots earlier in his career with later low-light work, in a 2018 interview.
Actor, Heartthrob, Superstar. Jyoti Prakash Sahoo, MyCityLinks, 15 July 2018; Uttam Mohanty on changing shooting conditions.

Colleagues’ recollections add another view of his practice. In Bijay Mandal’s 2020 retrospective, actor Jayaswami described his help in developing her work while keeping actors within their characters. Susant Mani recalled subtitling and mentorship; Pradeep Mohanty remembered borrowing Mahapatra’s 35mm camera rather than hiring one from Madras.
Exit of a cinematic giant. Bijay Mandal, OrissaPOST, 28 January 2020; named colleagues’ recollections.

A retrospective of Manmohan Mahapatra’s work lists *Rakta Tirtha Eram* (1997) and *Nua Sakala* (2000) for DDK Bhubaneswar. These are dates in the retrospective’s work list, not independently established broadcast dates.
Exit of a cinematic giant. Bijay Mandal, OrissaPOST, 28 January 2020; retrospective work list.
